Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1.
Heard Sri Apul Mishra, learned counsel for applicant and Sri Mankandey Singh, learned Brief Holder for State.

2. Applicant-Badan Singh has approached this Court by way of filing present bail application seeking enlargement on bail in Case No. 349 of 2021, arising out of Case Crime No. 13 of 2001,
under Sections 363, 366, 368, 376 IPC, Police Station Didauli, District Amroha, after rejection of his bail application vide order dated 28.11.2022 passed by Sessions Judge, Amroha.
3.
In the present case FIR was lodged way back in the year 2001 initially under Sections 363, 366 IPC against five named accused including applicant.

It was alleged that one of co-accused, namely,
Sanjeev and other co-accused have enticed victim and kidnapped her from lawful guardianship.
Present applicant is Mama of accused, Sanjeev.

Presently out of five named accused, two have already expired and except applicant, other two accused have been granted bail by this Court way Badan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154251137/
1 back in the year 2001.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for applicant submits that subsequently on the basis of statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. charge sheet was filed against applicant.

So far as applicant?s role is concerned, there was no allegation of rape against him in the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., however, victim has improved her version in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and attributed allegation of rape on applicant also.
Applicant has approached this Court by way of filing application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. challenging charge sheet and therein an interim order was passed in his favour.

Later on in terms of judgment passed by Supreme Court in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Private Limited and Another v. Central Bureau of Investigation (2018) 16 SCC 299 interim order vacated and trial is proceeded and presently charges are framed.

entities.text: Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Private Limited and Another v. Central Bureau of Investigation (2018) 16 SCC 299
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that applicant is also claiming parity since other co-accused have been granted bail including co-accused, Sanjeev, who was assigned main role, mainly on the ground that prosecution story does not find support from medical examination of victim.
Learned counsel further submits that presently applicant is a person aged about 67 years and he is in jail since 22.11.2022, therefore, he may be released on bail.
5. Learned Brief Holder appearing for State has opposed the prayer for bail.
He, however, has not disputed that co-accused, Sanjeev, who was assigned main role, has already been released on bail.

6. In the background of above referred submissions and facts, I find that there is merit in the argument of learned counsel for applicant and since other co-accused have already been released on bail on the ground that medical evidence does not prima facie support case of prosecution as also taking note that presently applicant is aged about 67 years old and trial has just commenced and at the stage of framing of charge, therefore, applicant, who is in jail since 22.11.2022, is entitled for bail.

7. However, applicant is directed to remain present on each and every date as and when required by Trial Court during trial and in case any application for exemption on vague ground is filed, the same shall be a ground for Trial Court to cancel bail immediately.

8. Let the applicant-Badan Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment or exemption from appearance on the date fixed in trial.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

sentences.text: 2 (iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of applicant,
if there is no other legal impediment.
9.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by Court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, Court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
10. The bail application is allowed.
11. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.
